neighbours.label: the verbs 'began / started / originated' telling where or when an event or practice first arose ('a festival that started in 2006')
fire: The custom of exchanging cards originated in nineteenth-century England.
The marathon, which started in 1897, is the oldest in the country.
Organized rugby in the region began with a few school teams.
The film festival started in a borrowed church hall in 1983.
Historians say the practice of tea drinking began in southern China.
The parade originated as a small gathering of local veterans.
The charity race began in 2004 with only forty runners.
Modern ballet started at the royal courts of France.
quiet: The custom of exchanging cards declined in nineteenth-century England.
The marathon, which ends at the harbour, is the oldest in the country.
Organized rugby in the region grew with a few school teams.
The film festival moved to a borrowed church hall in 1983.
Historians say the practice of tea drinking spread across southern China.
The parade ended as a small gathering of local veterans.
The charity race was held in 2004 with only forty runners.
Modern ballet flourished at the royal courts of France.
